text: Almost all good writing begins with terrible first efforts.
author: Anne Lamott

text: The scariest moment is always just before you start.
author: Stephen King

text: Writing is telepathy.
author: Stephen King

text: Read a lot and write a lot.
author: Stephen King

text: The road to hell is paved with adverbs.
author: Stephen King

text: You fail only if you stop writing.
author: Ray Bradbury

text: Quantity produces quality.
author: Ray Bradbury

text: Put one word after another.
author: Neil Gaiman

text: You can always edit a bad page. You can't edit a blank page.
author: Jodi Picoult

text: First forget inspiration. Habit is more dependable.
author: Octavia E. Butler

text: Writing is like driving at night in the fog.
author: E. L. Doctorow

text: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
author: Annie Dillard

text: Write to please just one person.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: Keep your hand moving.
author: Natalie Goldberg

text: You can't wait for inspiration. You have to go after it with a club.
author: Jack London

text: Good prose is like a windowpane.
author: George Orwell

text: Never use a long word where a short one will do.
author: George Orwell

text: Omit needless words.
author: William Strunk Jr.

text: We write to taste life twice, in the moment and in retrospect.
author: Anaïs Nin

text: I write entirely to find out what I'm thinking.
author: Joan Didion

text: I must keep to my own style and go on in my own way.
author: Jane Austen

text: All you have to do is write one true sentence.
author: Ernest Hemingway

text: The first draft is just you telling yourself the story.
author: Terry Pratchett

text: Write freely and as rapidly as possible and throw the whole thing on paper.
author: John Steinbeck

text: Writing is thinking on paper.
author: William Zinsser

text: Try to leave out the part that readers tend to skip.
author: Elmore Leonard

text: You have to write the book that wants to be written.
author: Madeleine L'Engle

text: A book must be the axe for the frozen sea inside us.
author: Franz Kafka

text: Start writing, no matter what.
author: Louis L'Amour

text: Words are, of course, the most powerful drug used by mankind.
author: Rudyard Kipling

text: No tears in the writer, no tears in the reader.
author: Robert Frost

text: The pen is mightier than the sword.
author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton
